senses.definition: Often with a prepositional phrase, or with to and an infinitive: showing a quick and ardent responsiveness or willingness; eager, enthusiastic, interested.
examples: I’m keen on computers.
I’m keen on you.
She’s keen to learn another language.

senses.definition: Fierce, intense, vehement.
examples: This boy has a keen appetite.

senses.definition: Having a fine edge or point; sharp.
Acute of mind, having or expressing mental acuteness; penetrating, sharp.
To continue in (a course or mode of action); to not intermit or fall from; to uphold or maintain.
examples: To keep silence; to keep possession.

senses.definition: To remain faithful to a given promise or word.
examples: To keep one's word; to keep one's promise.

senses.definition: To maintain possession of.
examples: I keep a small stock of painkillers for emergencies.
I only meant to lend him the shirt at first, but it looked better on him than me, so I told him to keep it.

senses.definition: To maintain the condition of; to preserve in a certain state.
examples: I keep my specimens under glass to protect them.
The abundance of squirrels kept the dogs running for hours.

senses.definition: One who keeps (retains) something.
examples: Finders keepers; losers weepers.

senses.definition: One who remains or keeps in a place or position.
A fruit or vegetable that keeps (remains good) for some time without spoiling.
A person or thing worth keeping.
Conformity or harmony.
examples: The songs are new but in keeping with tradition.
The foreground of this painting is not in keeping.

senses.definition: Charge or care.
Maintenance; support; provision; feed.
examples: The cattle have good keeping.

senses.definition: Only used in for keeps.
To know, perceive or understand.
Range of perception.
Knowledge, perception, or sight.
Range of sight.
A shepherd's staff.
A pole or pike.
Cunt.
To propel (a boat) using a pole.
An object designed to open and close a lock or to activate or deactivate something, especially a length of metal inserted into a narrow opening on the lock to which it is matched (keyed).
examples: This key is to the backdoor.
Insert the key into the lock (formal); put the key in the lock (informal).
Apartment key; room key; spare key.

senses.definition: A card or fob that electronically signals a lock to open.
examples: My hotel room key is a card.
The gym will give you a fob that opens the door.

senses.definition: A piece of information (e.g., a password or passphrase) used to encode or decode a message or messages.
A key bump (A portion of a recreational drug in powdered form that is snorted from a key or similar small object.).
examples: I saw him snort a key at the party.

senses.definition: A set of keys laid out in a gridlike pattern, used for typing on a typewriter, computer, etc.
A component of many instruments, including the piano, organ, and harpsichord, consisting of usually black and white keys that cause different tones to be produced when struck.
An electronic device containing a keyboard (preceding sense), especially one that is capable of producing musical sounds when the keys are played.
To type on a computer keyboard.
examples: Keyboarding is the part of this job I hate the most.

senses.definition: Keyboard.
An Ottoman sultan.
A noble or man of rank in various Muslim countries of Central Asia, including Afghanistan.
Synonym of caravanserai (particularly in Middle Eastern contexts).
Synonym of fonduk (“inn or hotel in Middle Eastern contexts”).
To strike or hit with the foot or other extremity of the leg.
examples: Did you kick your brother?
1895, George MacDonald, Lilith, Chapter XII: Friends and Foes, I was cuffed by the women and kicked by the men because I would not swallow it.

senses.definition: To make a sharp jerking movement of the leg, as to strike something.
examples: He enjoyed the simple pleasure of watching the kickline kick.

senses.definition: To direct to a particular place by a blow with the foot or leg.
examples: Kick the ball into the goal.

senses.definition: To eject summarily.
Empty with nothing left to smoke but ash.
Terrific, great (of clothes) smart, fashionable.
examples: A kicking pair of jeans.
A kicking party.

senses.definition: Alive, active (especially in the phrase alive and kicking).
examples: Still kicking at 89 years old.

senses.definition: Actively ongoing and enjoyable.
The action of the verb to kick.
examples: In boxing, kicking one's opponent is not allowed.

senses.definition: Shoes.
Commissary, or the balance of a commissary account.
examples: I’ve seen your kicks, inmate: you’ve got forty cents to your name.
He put a hundred bucks in your kicks each week.

senses.definition: A child, adolescent, or (loosely) a young adult.
examples: She's a kid. It's normal for her to have imaginary friends.

senses.definition: A person whose childhood took place in a particular time period or area.
examples: Only '90s kids will remember this toy.
He's been living in Los Angeles for years now, but he's a Florida kid.

senses.definition: One's son or daughter, regardless of age.
examples: This is Bobby, he is our youngest kid.

senses.definition: Used as a form of address for a child, teenager or young adult.
Joking, duping, or light-hearted deception.
The act of a goat giving birth.
An organ in the body that filters the blood, producing urine.
This organ (of an animal) cooked as food.
To put to death; to extinguish the life of.
examples: Smoking kills more people each year than alcohol and hard drugs combined.

senses.definition: To render inoperative.
examples: He killed the engine and turned off the headlights, but remained in the car, waiting.

senses.definition: To stop, cease, or render void; to terminate.
examples: The editor decided to kill the story.
The news that a hurricane had destroyed our beach house killed our plans to sell it.
My computer wouldn't respond until I killed some of the running processes.

senses.definition: To amaze, exceed, stun, or otherwise incapacitate.
examples: That night, she was dressed to kill.
That joke always kills me.

senses.definition: Deoxidized.
Inactivated.
One who or that which kills.
examples: There’s a killer on the loose.
My cat is a habitual bird killer.
Carbon monoxide is a silent killer.

senses.definition: That which causes stress or is extremely difficult, especially that which may cause failure at a task.
examples: That test was a killer.
The final hill in the race course was a killer.

senses.definition: Something that is so far ahead of its competition that it effectively kills off that competition.
examples: Digital streaming platforms are CD killers.

senses.definition: The killer whale.
That literally deprives of life; lethal, deadly, fatal.
That makes one ‘die’ with laughter; very funny.
The act of killing.
An instance of someone being killed.
A type, race or category; a group of entities that have common characteristics such that they may be grouped together.
examples: What kind of (a) person are you?
What kind of ice-cream would you like? There's chocolate, strawberry, and lemon.
Neither of them is the marrying kind.

senses.definition: A makeshift or otherwise atypical specimen.
examples: The opening served as a kind of window.

senses.definition: Goods or services used as payment, as e.g. in barter.
examples: In kind.
I don't have any money but I can pay in kind by washing the dishes.

senses.definition: Equivalent means used as response to an action.
examples: In kind.
I'll pay in kind for his insult.

senses.definition: Kind of; somewhat.
examples: I kinda hafta do this right now.
That’s kinda funny.

senses.definition: Yes in some respects but no in other respects.
examples: "Are you afraid of a little bit of rain?" "Kinda, yeah.".

senses.definition: A subspecies of baboon, Papio cynocephalus kindae, primarily found in Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zambia, and possibly western Tanzania.
Having a kind personality; kind, warm-hearted, sympathetic.
examples: A kindly old man sits on the park bench every afternoon feeding pigeons.

senses.definition: In a kind manner, out of kindness.
examples: He kindly offered to take us to the station in his car.

senses.definition: In a favourable way.
Used to make a polite request: please.
examples: Kindly refrain from walking on the grass.
May we request that patrons kindly take their seats.

senses.definition: The state of being kind.
examples: Jamie's kindness is legendary, so much that people have taken advantage of her.

senses.definition: An instance of kind or charitable behaviour.
examples: How can I thank you for your many kindnesses?
Do me a kindness and leave.
I'm going to turn a blind eye to this misdemeanour, out of the kindness of my heart.

senses.definition: A male monarch; a man who heads a monarchy; in an absolute monarchy, the supreme ruler of his nation.
examples: Henry VIII was the king of England from 1509 to 1547.
Charles the third became the new king of England from 2022.

senses.definition: The monarch with the most power and authority in a monarchy, regardless of sex.
A powerful or majorly influential person; someone who holds the preeminent position.
examples: Howard Stern styled himself as the "king of all media".

senses.definition: Something that has a preeminent position.
examples: In times of financial panic, cash is king.

senses.definition: A realm having a king or queen as its actual or nominal sovereign.
A realm, region, or conceptual space where something is dominant.
examples: The kingdom of thought.
The kingdom of the dead.

senses.definition: A rank in the classification of organisms, below domain and above phylum; a taxon at that rank (e.g. the plant kingdom, the animal kingdom).
A pair of kings (playing cards).
A drinking game that uses playing cards.
To touch with the lips or press the lips against, usually to show love or affection or passion, or as part of a greeting.
To (cause to) touch lightly or slightly; to come into contact.
examples: The nearside of the car just kissed a parked truck as he took the corner at high speed.
His ball kissed the black into the corner pocket.

senses.definition: Of two or more people, to touch each other's lips together, usually to express love or affection or passion.
A touch with the lips, usually to express love or affection, or as a greeting.
A circular wooden vessel, made of hooped staves.
A kind of basket made especially from straw of rushes, especially for holding fish; by extension, the contents of such a basket or similar container, used as a measure of weight.
examples: He was pushing a barrow on the fish dock, wheeling aluminium kits which, when full, each contain 10 stone of fish.

senses.definition: A collection of items forming the equipment of a soldier, carried in a knapsack.
Any collection of items needed for a specific purpose, especially for use by a workman, or personal effects packed for travelling.
examples: Always carry a good first-aid kit.

senses.definition: A room or area for preparing food.
examples: We cook in the kitchen.

senses.definition: Cuisine; style of cooking.
The nape of a person's hairline, often referring to its uncombed or "nappy" look.
The percussion section of an orchestra.
In humans, the joint or the region of the joint in the middle part of the leg between the thigh and the shank.
examples: Penny was wearing a miniskirt, so she skinned her exposed knees when she fell.

senses.definition: In the horse and allied animals, the carpal joint, corresponding to the wrist in humans.
The tarsal joint, uniting the tarsometatarsus and the tibiotarsus (homologous to the human ankle).
The joint uniting the tibiotarsus and the femur, typically hidden beneath plumage.

A utensil or a tool designed for cutting, consisting of a flat piece of hard material, usually steel or other metal (the blade), usually sharpened on one edge, attached to a handle. The blade may be pointed for piercing.
examples: He was looking for a knife to chop some steak.

senses.definition: A weapon designed with the aforementioned specifications intended for slashing or stabbing but too short to be called a sword; a dagger.
Any blade-like part in a tool or a machine designed for cutting, such as that of a chipper.
To cut with a knife.
An armored and mounted warrior of the Middle Ages.
examples: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table.

senses.definition: A person on whom a knighthood has been conferred by a monarch.
A brave, chivalrous and honorable man devoted to a noble cause or love interest.
A chess piece, often in the shape of a horse's head, that is moved two squares in one direction and one at right angles to that direction in a single move, leaping over any intervening pieces.
An abrupt rapping sound, as from an impact of a hard object against wood.
A sharp impact.
examples: He took a knock on the head.

senses.definition: A criticism.
A blow or setback.
To perceive the truth or factuality of; to be certain of; to be certain that.
examples: I know that I’m right and you’re wrong.

senses.definition: To be or become aware or cognizant.
examples: Did you know Michelle and Jack were getting divorced? ― Yes, I knew.
Malware's sometimes been known to sit dormant for a long time.

senses.definition: To be aware of; to be cognizant of.
examples: Did you know Michelle and Jack were getting divorced? ― Yes, I knew.
She knows where I live.
I knew he was upset, but I didn't understand why.

senses.definition: To be acquainted or familiar with; to have encountered.
examples: I know your mother, but I've never met your father.
Borja, do you know Pilar? - Sure, we've actually met before.
I got to know her during the pandemic, so we've known each other for years now.

senses.definition: Possessing knowledge or understanding; knowledgeable, intelligent.
Deliberate, wilful.
Shrewd or showing clever awareness; discerning.

senses.definition: Suggestive of private knowledge or understanding.
The fact of knowing about something; general understanding or familiarity with a subject, place, situation etc.
examples: His knowledge of Iceland was limited to what he'd seen on the Travel Channel.

senses.definition: Awareness of a particular fact or situation; a state of having been informed or made aware of something.
Intellectual understanding; the state of appreciating truth or information.

senses.definition: Familiarity or understanding of a particular skill, branch of learning etc.
examples: Does your friend have any knowledge of hieroglyphs, perchance?

senses.definition: Identified as a specific type; famous, renowned.
examples: He was a known pickpocket.

senses.definition: Accepted, familiar, researched.

senses.definition: Any fact or situation which is known or familiar.
examples: You have to tell the knowns from the unknowns.

senses.definition: A constant or variable the value of which is already determined.
A set of four identical tiles.
A call declaring the formation of such a set.
A narrow arm or channel of the sea between an island and the mainland, or between two islands.
